name: LSTM (long short-term memory)
summary: A recurrent neural network with gated memory that can learn long-range patterns in sequences.
inputs: Sequences (windows) of one or more variables; optional exogenous inputs.
outputs: Next-step or multi-step predictions, or sequence classifications.

data_requirements.min_observations: Many thousands of windows or many related series

assumptions: Enough training sequences to fit many parameters
math_summary: A recurrent cell with an internal memory state controlled by gates (input, output and, in later variants, forget); the additive memory path lets error flow over long time lags without vanishing.
when_to_use: Many related sequences or long histories
Non-linear temporal patterns with exogenous inputs
when_not_to_use: Short, single financial series (high overfitting risk; strong classical baselines)
pitfalls: Look-ahead leakage in scaling and windowing
Comparing only to naive baselines instead of ARIMA/ETS/boosting

compute.complexity: O(T * h^2) per sequence for hidden size h; sequential over time.
compute.hardware: Small models train on CPU; GPU helpful for large data.

applicability.use_case: Hourly electricity load forecasting with weather covariates
Sequence models of trade flows or shipping activity

theory.rationale: Sound motivation for gradient flow (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber 1997) but no statistical guarantees; behaviour on small noisy series is not well characterised.

ease.rationale: Needs windowing, scaling without leakage, architecture and training choices; GPU helps at scale.
